Each stone is set in a hand-cut sawtooth bezel accented with silver raindrops, twisted rope borders, and intimate hand-applied wire-work scrolls over an oxidized background. Given the lack of a maker's mark but the presence of the "STERLING" stamp and brushed interior, this bracelet was likely produced for a Southwest trading post or gallery during the 1970's turquoise boom. The "STERLING" punch is a standard commercial steel punch used widely by Navajo silversmiths from the mid-1960's onwards. The fine, uniform horizontal brush marks on the inside are characteristic of rolled sterling sheet stick finished with a fine abrasive pad, which was available from the 1950's onward. det.desc: This document is a World War II-era dual-language transit pass (Bescheinigung / Laisser-Passer) issued in Arcachon, France, on July 19, 1940. Document Details • Name of Holder: Pierre Lejuge • Destination: Cap Ferret • Mode of Transport: Boat (Bateau, permanent) • Nationality: French (Française) • Issuing Authorities: • German Military Authority: Signed by a Major and Ortskommandant (local commander), featuring an official German military stamp/eagle. • French Police Authority: Issued by the Police Commissioner (Le Commissaire de Police) in Arcachon on July 19, 1940, with an official stamp. Historical Context Issued just weeks after the Fall of France and the signing of the armistice in June 1940, this pass allowed a French civilian (Pierre Lejuge) to travel by boat to the Arcachon Bay peninsula of Cap Ferret under dual oversight of the German occupying forces and the local Vichy-controlled French police.
